'''''Arenga''''' is a genus of [[Arecaceae|palms]], native to [[Southeast Asia]], southern [[China]], [[New Guinea]], and northern [[Australia]].<ref name=uioiusdfous89df0usdfusdaf4tr24>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=14659 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=102521 Flora of China, Vol. 23 Page 151, <big>桄榔属</big> guang lang shu, ''Arenga'' Labillardière, Bull. Sci. Soc. Philom. Paris. 2: 162. 1800. ]</ref> They are small to medium-sized palms, growing to 2–20 m tall, with pinnate [[leaf|leaves]] 2–12 m long.<ref>Govaerts, R. & Dransfield, J. (2005). World Checklist of Palms: 1–223. The Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.</ref><ref>Henderson, A. (2009). Palms of Southern Asia: 1–197. Princeton university press, Princeton and Oxford.</ref> Arenga palms can grow in areas with little sunlight and relatively infertile soil.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.reuters.com/article/idUS115545511820110718| title = The Amazing Arenga Sugar Palm| website = [[Reuters]]}} </ref>
